scheme_name: One Time Traffic Challan Settlement Scheme, 2026

percent_by_class.compoundable_offences: about 50% relief, per the notification's own schedule

order_ref: Notification No. 3261 dated 30 April 2026 (Cabinet-approved, e-gazette published; recorded in the Patna High Court orders of 4 May and 23 June 2026 in CWJC No. 20071 of 2025)
note: Bihar notified a one-time settlement on 30 April 2026 and first ran it at the 9 May 2026 National Lok Adalat, where the High Court records that about 36,722 cases were disposed of. The Patna High Court's judgment of 23 June 2026 states that 'the amount of fines prescribed for compoundable traffic challans have been reduced by about 50% and are detailed accordingly in the said notification' — so the relief is not a flat 50% cut but a schedule of amounts, and it applies to compoundable offences only. The same judgment records that the notification 'extends only to the financial year 2026-27', which ends 31 March 2027, and that the government may consider extending it year on year. The notification's own text (Notification No. 3261) is still not published anywhere we can reach. A Regional Transport Authority (Saran division) circular dated 6 May 2026 confirms the scheme by name and its use for challans pending over 90 days at the 9 May 2026 Lok Adalat, but does not itself state the 50% figure or the window dates — so the percentage and duration remain evidenced only through the High Court record. The scheme is still running: press reports confirm a further National Lok Adalat on 12 September 2026 again offered the same 50%-of-pending-amount settlement for challans older than 90 days (overloading challans excluded), with advance filing at District Transport Offices from 7-11 September 2026. Confirm the amount shown against your own challan on the official portal before paying. Re-checked 16 October 2026: the Patna High Court judgments at the cited Indian Kanoon links and the RTA (Saran) circular PDF still resolve with the same text, and no newer press report or notification was found beyond the 12 September 2026 Lok Adalat round already recorded here — the 50%-of-pending-amount relief, FY 2026-27 window, and compoundable-offences-only scope stand unchanged. Re-checked 19 October 2026: all three Patna High Court orders (20 April, 4 May and 23 June 2026, CWJC No. 20071 of 2025) still resolve at the cited Indian Kanoon links with the same text — the 23 June order still states the fines were 'reduced by about 50%' and that the notification 'extends only to the financial year 2026-27', and still records the 36,722 disposals at the 9 May sitting. The RTA (Saran) circular PDF and the patnapress.com report both still resolve; the press report still describes only the 12 September 2026 Lok Adalat round already recorded here, with no mention of a further sitting or any change to the 50% figure. No newer notification or press coverage found. Facts unchanged. Facts unchanged.
